recipe: Upgrade to React 18.3 before upgrading to React 19 to identify issues early.
trigger_condition: When upgrading a React application from 18.x to 19.x
evidence: We recommend upgrading to React 18.3 first to help identify any issues before upgrading to React 19.

recipe: Use the `codemod` command instead of `react-codemod` when running React 19 migration codemods.
trigger_condition: When running React 19 codemods to automate migration of deprecated APIs
evidence: we recommend using the `codemod` command instead of the `react-codemod` because it runs faster, handles more complex code migrations, and provides better support for TypeScript.

recipe: Migrate function component `propTypes` to TypeScript interfaces and replace `defaultProps` with ES6 default parameters.
trigger_condition: When a function component uses `propTypes` or `defaultProps` from the prop-types package
evidence: If you're using `propTypes`, we recommend migrating to TypeScript or another type-checking solution.

recipe: Install `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` at version 19.0.0 when upgrading a TypeScript React project to React 19.
trigger_condition: When upgrading a TypeScript React project to React 19
evidence: If you're using TypeScript, you also need to update the types.

recipe: Use `onUncaughtError` and `onCaughtError` options in `createRoot` or `hydrateRoot` to handle render errors that are no longer re-thrown.
trigger_condition: When production error reporting relied on React re-throwing render errors
evidence: we've added new methods to `createRoot` and `hydrateRoot` for custom error handling

recipe: Replace Legacy Context (`contextTypes`/`getChildContext`) with `React.createContext()` and `contextType` in class components.
trigger_condition: When a class component uses `contextTypes` or `getChildContext`
evidence: you'll need to migrate to the new `contextType` API

recipe: Replace string refs with ref callbacks in class components.
trigger_condition: When a class component uses string refs like `ref='input'`
evidence: you'll need to migrate to ref callbacks

recipe: Install `react-shallow-renderer` directly and import `ShallowRenderer` from it instead of using `react-test-renderer/shallow`.
trigger_condition: When a test imports `ShallowRenderer` from `react-test-renderer/shallow`
evidence: we're removing `react-test-render/shallow` to prefer installing the package directly

recipe: Enable the new JSX transform in React 19 to support ref-as-prop and JSX speed improvements.
trigger_condition: When upgrading to React 19 and the app uses the legacy JSX transform
evidence: In React 19, we're adding additional improvements like using ref as a prop and JSX speed improvements that require the new transform.

evidence: In React 19, you'll need to migrate to using `root.unmount()`.

recipe: Access the ref via `element.props.ref` instead of `element.ref` when working with React elements in TypeScript.
trigger_condition: Your TypeScript code accesses `element.ref` on a React element and you are upgrading to React 19.
evidence: React 19 supports [`ref` as a prop](/blog/2024/04/25/react-19#ref-as-a-prop), so we're deprecating the `element.ref` in place of `element.props.ref`.

evidence: and we now recommend using a modern testing library instead.

recipe: Remove any code in your application or library that depends on React internals (e.g., `SECRET_INTERNALS`-prefixed exports) to keep future upgrades unblocked.
trigger_condition: Your codebase accesses React internal APIs (e.g., `SECRET_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED` exports) and you are upgrading to React 19.
evidence: The recommendation is to remove any code that depends on internals.
